solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Setback when there's commercial break — it could be interrupting play

indicators.note: the commercial break here is taken literally: the advert breaks into the setback word

parts.note: a blight is a setback or spoiling influence
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A television viewer grumbles that the adverts have interrupted the game they were watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like part of 'commercial break' but signals the container. The play is cricket: umpires stop a match when the light is too poor.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, poor light is a common reason for umpires to suspend the game, so it interrupts play.

clue.text: Playin' in the street with a boot

definitions.meaning: performing music outdoors for coins, with the dropped g
a high laced boot, especially one worn by ancient tragic actors

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Playin'' licenses the dropped G of busking.
explanation.definitionFit: A buskin is a calf-length boot; the other sense is street performing with the final g clipped.

clue.text: It's not so dry? Check

definitions.meaning: more moist, the comparative of moist
something that restrains, like a piano mute or a stove's flue plate

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the comparative of moist; the other is a device or influence that restrains.

clue.text: The irony that's funny on paper

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Irony that is amusing only when written down.
explanation.definitionFit: 'On paper' is an idiom for something that works as a plan but untested in practice.

clue.text: Man moans — hope is abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A man laments that all hope has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'abandoned' as given up; it signals a wild rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the scientific species name for human beings, mankind.

clue.text: Make sense of sound

definitions.meaning: to understand or work out something puzzling
to measure the depth of water, as a sailor does with a line

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to comprehend; the other is to take a depth sounding, a fathom being six feet of water.

clue.text: Breaking down when female's gone, languishing

indicators.note: gone means the letter for female has left the longer word

parts.note: failing means breaking down
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A machine stops working once the woman operating it leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sick and weak is a state of decline, close to languishing.

clue.text: What unusual outgrowth may be seen in tree?

indicators.note: unusual means the word what is set out in a strange order

parts.note: a horn is a bony outgrowth

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what odd growth might appear on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a thorny hedgerow tree of the rose family, also called may.

clue.text: Mark meeting pouring rain had to get soaked

indicators.note: pouring rain is rain in a torrent, so its letters are tumbled about

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat, so had means ate

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark, out in pouring rain, ends up drenched.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left to steep in a seasoned liquid is steeped or soaked in it.

clue.text: Sequence of four notes from past

parts.note: the sol-fa notes so, me, ti, me in a row
me, the third note of the sol-fa scale
ti, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
me again, the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical phrase of four notes borrowed from an earlier era.
explanation.walkthrough: The notes are tonic sol-fa syllables (doh, ray, me, fah, so, la, ti), strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means former, as in 'a sometime teacher', someone belonging to the past.

clue.text: Female subordinate's bloomer

parts.note: lower in rank means subordinate

explanation.surface: A junior woman in the office has made an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake, but here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's blossom is something that blooms, so a bloomer in the literal sense.

clue.text: Rebel taking on board a golfer and a football team

indicators.note: taking on board means holding inside, so the golfer sits within the rebel

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
Ernie Els, the South African golfer

explanation.surface: A rebel recruits a golfer and a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea FC is a London club playing in the Premier League.

clue.text: I bond almost entirely with professional killers

indicators.note: almost means the word for bond loses only its final letter

parts.note: cement bonds things together

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of getting on very well with hired assassins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' drops the last T of CEMENT. 'Ice' is slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang to ice someone is to murder them, so icemen are hired assassins.

clue.text: Country falling short repeatedly in respect of good health!

indicators.note: repeatedly means the shortened word is written out twice in a row
falling short means the country's name stops before its final letter

parts.note: China is a country

explanation.surface: A toast proposed for a nation's health that keeps failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' cuts the last A from CHINA, and 'repeatedly' doubles what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal drinking toast, said when raising a glass to someone's health.

clue.text: See 4
Blandishments from elder maybe to get a class enthralled

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so the tree holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: the elder is an example of a tree
CL is an abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: A senior person charms a class into rapt attention with flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elder' suggests an older person; here it is the shrub-like tree, and 'enthralled' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively it means cloying, sugary talk, the sort of sweet flattery used to coax someone.

clue.text: Document with wiggle he ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the word he is left out of the longer word

parts.note: to writhe is to twist and wiggle

explanation.surface: A paper that he paid no attention to, despite a wriggle.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal order issued in written form by a court is a formal document.

clue.text: Ploy was first to get leaked

parts.note: a trick is a ploy
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A scheme that was the first to be leaked to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that escaped slowly in a thin stream is said to have dribbled or leaked out.

clue.text: Begged to have existence as escaped prisoner

parts.note: to be is to exist
a fugitive is sought by the police

explanation.surface: Pleading to live as a convict on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: An escaped prisoner is one who is being searched for, so 'sought'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old past tense form of beseech, meaning pleaded urgently.

clue.text: Below summit dash up for a drink

indicators.note: below puts the second piece under the first in this down answer

parts.note: the brow is the top of a hill

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: elan is dash or flair

explanation.surface: Racing up from below the summit to get a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dark, sweet British beer, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Oxford college without love or money

indicators.note: without means the letter for love is removed from the college name

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: An Oxford college left with neither romance nor cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money' looks like part of a lament but is the definition: the currency of Cambodia.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the currency unit of Cambodia, so a kind of money.

clue.text: Sculptures, say, suitable for putting around close

indicators.note: around means the word for suitable is placed on both sides of the other word

parts.note: fit means suitable
near means close

explanation.surface: Statues judged appropriate to place around a cathedral close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' suggests a cathedral precinct but is just 'near'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpture is one example of the visual arts produced for beauty, alongside painting.

clue.text: Writer is a revolutionary wanting endless progress

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the words is a are read backwards
wanting its end means the word for progress loses its final letter

parts.note: to move is to progress

explanation.surface: An author who is a radical frustrated by a lack of advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a noun for the writer but turns IS A to ASI.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific American science fiction author.

clue.text: Wight is island around which there's anger

indicators.note: the island has the word for anger placed all round it

parts.note: wrath is anger

explanation.surface: The Isle of Wight is said to be an island surrounded by fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wight' suggests the Isle of Wight off England's south coast; here it is an old word for a ghostly being.
explanation.definitionFit: A wight is an old word for a creature, often a ghostly spectre, as is a wraith.

clue.text: See nut's ridiculous computer collection

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, so the letters are arranged absurdly

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a silly crank's computer hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an early worldwide network of discussion newsgroups, a collection of computer forums.

clue.text: Argue or maybe sound joyful in the course of puzzles

definitions.note: a verb; the answer is its present participle form, cross swords

indicators.note: in the course of means the singing goes inside the word for puzzles

parts.note: crosswords are puzzles
to sing is to sound joyful

explanation.surface: Solvers either quarrel or happily hum while working through their puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the course of' signals a container; the surface hides it in a phrase about time.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is an idiom for having a dispute, figuratively a duel of words.

clue.text: See 25
It has ace tomb, not very English!

definitions.text: It has ace tomb, not very English!

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

indicators.note: not means the letters for very and English are removed from the tomb word

parts.note: a grave is a tomb

explanation.surface: A boast about a superb tomb that is pointedly foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the city: it has the Taj Mahal, a superb tomb, and is far from English, being in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city in Uttar Pradesh is home to the Taj Mahal, the world's most famous tomb.

clue.text: Sort of plant to stick in the shade

indicators.note: in means the word for stick is placed inside the word for shade

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered, shady side
gum is to stick

explanation.surface: Instructions to fix a plant somewhere out of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas, beans and lentils belong to the pod-bearing family of plants.

clue.text: Relationship through paternal line in a good country

parts.note: a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A family connection through the father's side in a fine land.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a technical term for kinship traced only through male ancestors.

clue.text: Case of person living in country wanting new leader

indicators.note: wanting a new leader means the word's first letter must be replaced by another

parts.note: a native is someone living in, or from, a country

explanation.surface: A legal case involving a resident whose nation wants fresh leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a lawsuit but is the grammatical case. NATIVE's first letter is swapped for a new one; the definition says which.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar it is the noun case marking an indirect object, as in Latin and German.

clue.text: Don't get hold of THIS old group

definitions.meaning: the opposite of grabbing this item is grabbing the other one, so a phrase meaning 'have the other'
a British boy band of the 1990s

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals on THIS invite the contrast: not this, but that. Take That is a British pop group formed in 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the opposite instruction to grabbing this; the other names a well-known 1990s pop band.
